title: Vercel Launched Experimental Board to Coordinate Tasks Across Humans and Coding Agents
gist: Vercel launched Vercel Board, an experimental headless message board where humans and multiple coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Mastra, LangChain and others) coordinate leased tasks with dependencies, synced to Slack, GitHub and Linear; Vercel says v0's software factory, rebuilt on Board, merges over 50% of its pull requests. It enters a crowded agent-coordination space alongside GitHub Agent HQ, Linear, Claude Code agent teams and the Agent2Agent protocol.

insights.claim: Vercel launched Vercel Board, an experimental headless message board on which Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, eve, fx, Mastra and LangChain agents can work alongside humans as if they were a single harness.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Vercel is positioning itself as a neutral coordination layer across rival coding-agent vendors.

insights.claim: Vercel Board agents read and write via the vercel board CLI or the @vercel/board JavaScript SDK, name themselves with --as or BOARD_PROFILE, but still act with the operator's or project's credentials.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Agent identity is cosmetic; access control still rides on human credentials — a governance consideration.
insights.locator: Each Vercel team gets a default board

insights.claim: In Vercel Board a task is a thread with board-kept state: a worker claims it with a lease of up to five minutes that must be renewed, expired claims return the task to the queue, and concurrent claims resolve with one success and one task_claimed failure.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Applies classic distributed work-queue semantics to multi-agent software development.
insights.locator: A task is a thread whose state the board keeps

insights.claim: Vercel Board tasks can declare dependencies so a review waits for its fix while independent work runs in parallel, and watchers can wake a Vercel deployment on replies or label changes so no process must stay running.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Event-driven wakeups tie agent coordination to Vercel's serverless deployment model, driving platform usage.

insights.claim: Vercel Board sync via Vercel Connect attaches channels to Slack and Linear bidirectionally and imports GitHub pull requests and issues, and sandboxPolicy() can grant agents in a Vercel Sandbox limited board access without placing a credential inside the sandbox.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Deep integration with existing work tools lowers adoption friction for teams running agents.

insights.claim: Vercel's documentation warns that Board grants do not apply on Slack, GitHub or Linear, so a private Slack channel synced into an open board channel becomes readable by the whole Vercel team.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Permission gaps in agent-coordination sync are a data-leak risk for enterprise adopters.

insights.claim: Vercel says it rebuilt v0's software factory on Board and that the factory now merges over 50% of its pull requests.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: A vendor-reported metric for agent-generated code merge rates; useful benchmark but self-reported.
insights.quote: the factory now merges over 50% of its pull requests
insights.locator: Vercel says it rebuilt v0's software factory

insights.claim: Agent-coordination alternatives to Vercel Board include open-source self-hostable OpenCrawl, GitHub Agent HQ assigning issues to Copilot, Claude or Codex, Linear's cloud coding agent, Claude Code agent teams sharing a task list, and the Agent2Agent protocol for standardized delegation.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Multi-agent orchestration is becoming a contested platform layer among GitHub, Linear, Anthropic and Vercel.

insights.claim: Developer reaction to Vercel Board included demand for a self-hosted open-source alternative (Austin King registered openboard.lol for one) and praise for requiring evidence such as an attached pull request before a task is marked done.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Open-source clones may emerge quickly, limiting Vercel's lock-in.
insights.quote: Same rule my agents run on: no saying 'done' without the evidence.
